description: Render a Chart.js-style chart from structured labels and datasets and return a public CDN link instead of image bytes. Use this tool when: you need to embed a chart in an HTML page, markdown document, or email via an src attribute; you need to pass a chart URL to another tool or API; you want a PDF (Pro or Agency); you want to avoid sending large base64 image blobs in the conversation. Do NOT use this tool when: you want the image displayed inline in chat → use render_chart instead; you have raw or natural-language data → use render_chart_ai instead; you need a full branded card → use render_card_url instead. Behavior: this tool makes a remote API call to Chart-Output, may consume render credits, and returns a publicly accessible CDN link. Free-plan images carry a small watermark. Datasets keep every key you send (fill, tension, borderDash, stack, yAxisID, a dataset-level type for bar + line mixes, per-dataset datalabels). Data items can be numbers, null (a gap), {x, y} or [from, to] (floating bars). Returns: a plain text string containing a single HTTPS link to the rendered chart (e.g. "https://cdn.chart-output.com/..."). The link is publicly accessible. Errors (the message is plain text and keeps the API's details): 400 — invalid spec; every failing field is listed with its path. 401 — API key missing or invalid. 402 — monthly allowance used up; do NOT retry, tell the user (the message has the reset date and an upgrade link). 403 — the plan does not include something you used (pdf, a size above the plan cap, a brand kit over the limit); do NOT retry the same request, tell the user. 404 — unknown brand slug (the message lists the available ones). 429 — rate-limited; wait for Retry-After. Network error — chart-output.com is unreachable or timed out. Example: render_chart_url({ type: "line", labels: ["Jan","Feb","Mar"], datasets: [{ label: "MAU", data: [12000, 18000, 24000] }], title: "Monthly Active Users" }) → "https://cdn.chart-output.com/abc123.png"

alt_text.description: true returns a free template description of the chart (alt text) with the result. "ai" asks for a written description, which uses the plan's AI alt-text allowance and falls back to the template with a warning when it is used up. Useful when the reader cannot see the image.

annotations.description: Event markers. Works only on line and bar charts with a category x-axis (not pie, doughnut, radar or polarArea, and not options.indexAxis "y"). Shapes: {x: "Mar", label: "Spring sale"} (vertical line), {x_start: "May", x_end: "Jun", style: "band", label: "Outage"} (shaded band), {y: 30000, label: "Target"} (horizontal line). Labels are cut at 30 characters. At most 10 per chart on Free, 25 on paid plans (more is a 400). Markers that cannot be placed are skipped and reported as warnings.

brand.description: Slug of a saved brand kit (call list_brand_kits to see them), for example "acme-dark". Applies the kit's palette, fonts and logo. Colors you send yourself (dataset colors, theme) win over the kit. An unknown slug is a 404 that lists the real ones. Preset kits (obsidian, linen, polar, studio, ember, harbor) go in extensions.brandKitId instead.

colorblind_safe.description: true switches to a color-blind-safe palette.

dataLabels.description: true draws value labels on the chart. Number style (prefix, suffix, signed, share, maximumFractionDigits) goes in options.plugins.datalabels.numberFormat; pass options through extensions.

datasets.description: Array of data series (1–20). Each entry represents one line, bar group, or set of slices. Other Chart.js dataset keys (pointBackgroundColor, barPercentage, datalabels, …) pass through. Example: [{ label: "Revenue", data: [100, 200, 150], backgroundColor: "#4F81BD" }]. For pie/doughnut, use one dataset with an array of backgroundColor values.

backgroundColor.description: Fill color(s). Pass a single CSS color string for bar/line series or an array of colors (one per slice) for pie/doughnut. Accepts hex, rgb(), rgba(), or named colors. In a stacked bar, series after the first with a plain #rrggbb color are drawn at 70% opacity; use rgba(r,g,b,1) for the exact color. Example: "#4F81BD" or ["#FF6384","#36A2EB","#FFCE56"].

borderColor.description: Border/stroke color(s). Same format as backgroundColor. Commonly used for line charts to set the line color. Example: "#2c5f8a".

borderDash.description: Dashed line pattern, e.g. [6, 4]. The second line series is dashed automatically; set [] to keep it solid.

borderRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels for bar chart bars. Use 4–8 for a modern rounded look. Ignored for non-bar chart types. Example: 6.

data.description: Values, one per label entry (same length as the top-level labels array, up to 1000). Each item is a number, null (a gap), {x, y}, or [from, to] (a floating bar, used for ranges, bridges and waterfalls). Example: [12000, 15000, 18000, 22000].

fill.description: Line charts: true fills the area under the line (an area chart).

label.description: Series name shown in the chart legend. Example: "Revenue" or "Active Users". Omit for single-series pie/doughnut charts.

pointRadius.description: Line charts: point size in pixels; 0 hides points.

stack.description: Bar charts: datasets with the same stack id are stacked together. Example: "a".

type.description: Dataset-level type for a bar + line mix (usually with a second yAxisID). Example: "line".

yAxisID.description: Which y axis the series uses, e.g. "y1" for a second axis in a bar + line mix.

extensions.description: Optional extra POST /api/v1/render fields, merged first and then overridden by type/labels/datasets/width/height/format. Shapes: header {eyebrow?, title?, subtitle?, badge? {text, backgroundColor?, color?, borderRadius?, position? "start"|"end"}, align?, logoUrl?}, kpiStrip [{label, value, color?}] (max 12, value is a string), footer {left?, right?, borderTop?}, theme {palette?, backgroundColor?, fontFamily?, fontSize?, gridColor?, mode? "light"|"dark", textPrimary?, textSecondary?} (an object, never a string), legend, border {color, width}, borderRadius, backgroundColor, padding, brandKitId, brand, options (partial Chart.js options). Do not send returnUrl.

footer.description: Card footer: {left?, right?, borderTop?}. There is no text field.

format.description: Output format of the file at the returned URL. "png" (default) — lossless, universally supported. "jpeg" — smaller file, lossy. "webp" — modern, compact. "svg" — scalable vector, ideal for web embeds. "pdf" — needs a Pro or Agency plan.

header.description: Card header: {eyebrow?, title?, subtitle? (each up to 200 chars), badge? {text, backgroundColor?, color?, borderRadius?, position? "start"|"end"} (an object, never a string), align? "left"|"center", logoUrl? (https), logoHeight?, logoAlign? "left"|"right"}. Any header, kpiStrip, footer, border or legend turns the output into a card (always PNG).

height.description: Output image height in pixels. Range: 100–4000. Default: 400. The longest edge × scale must fit your plan: 1200 px on Free, 3000 px on Pro and Agency (the API answers 403 above that). Use 400 for landscape, 500–600 for square or portrait charts.

kpiStrip.description: KPI row under the header: up to 12 items {label, value, color?}. value is a string such as "$29,840". There is no delta field.

labels.description: Category labels or x-axis tick labels (1–1000). Keep the array the same length as every dataset's data array (a mismatch is not rejected by default; the chart renders with gaps). Example: ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"] or ["Product A", "Product B"].

lang.description: BCP 47 language tag for generated text such as alt text, e.g. "en".

repair.description: Opt in to the API's own repair mode (sent as repair_mode). "safe" fixes harmless problems without losing data (sorts {x,y} points, normalises colors, applies a default palette) and reports each repair. "off" only checks and returns a precise error with a suggested fix; it is the only way to catch labels/data length mismatches. Leave unset for the normal behavior. Set "safe" when you are unsure about your data. If an error says a decision is needed, ask the user.

scale.description: Pixel density multiplier for sharper (retina) output, 1–4. Default: 1. The longest edge × scale must fit your plan: 1200 px on Free, 3000 px on Pro and Agency (the API answers 403 above that). On a Free plan keep scale at 1 unless width and height are both 600 or less.

textScale.description: Makes all text on a card bigger (header, legend, ticks, KPIs, footer), 1–2. Use for small charts or low vision.

title.description: Optional chart title rendered at the top of the image. Example: "Q1–Q4 Revenue 2024". Omit if untitled.

type.description: Chart type. Use "bar" or "line" for time-series and comparisons. Use "pie" or "doughnut" for proportions (best with ≤7 categories). Use "radar" for multi-axis comparisons. Use "polarArea" for relative magnitude. Example: "line".

width.description: Output image width in pixels. Range: 100–4000. Default: 800. The longest edge × scale must fit your plan: 1200 px on Free, 3000 px on Pro and Agency (the API answers 403 above that). Use 1200 for widescreen, 400 for thumbnail embeds.

name: render_chart_url
